title: Prescriptions Refund Schedule: Unpaid Value of Declined Controlled Units
content:
For a Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Schedule V Controlled Prescription, Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription or Schedule II Controlled Prescription class, the controlled unpaid value is the value of the declined owed units that the controlled decline credit returns. It follows how the controlled short fill was paid and what the patient holds under Prescription Insurance on File and Savings & Copay Assistance Programs.

## The three methods, in order

1. **Commercial Copay Plan.** When the controlled short fill was billed to insurance and the patient's active coverage under Prescription Insurance on File is a Commercial Copay Plan, whose flat copay is reset by whole weeks of therapy, the unpaid value is the patient pay multiplied by 7 for every whole week of therapy in the owed units, and divided by the prescription's written days supply. The owed units are turned into days at the prescription's written days supply per written quantity; only whole weeks of 7 days count.
2. **Savings Club.** When the controlled short fill was settled under a discount program and the patient holds an active Kestrel Rx Savings Club Individual or Kestrel Rx Savings Club Family membership under Savings & Copay Assistance Programs, the unpaid value is the patient pay less that membership's value-list 30-day price for every started 30 days of the short fill's days supply dispensed.
3. **Otherwise** the unpaid value is the patient pay multiplied by the owed units and divided by the units dispensed plus the owed units.

## Figures (hypothetical)

**Method 1** — patient pay 28.00, written 30 units for 30 days (1 daily unit):

| Owed units | Owed days | Whole weeks | Unpaid value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 6 | 0 | 0.00 |
| 7 | 7 | 1 | 28.00 multiplied by 7, divided by 30: 6.5333 |
| 15 | 15 | 2 | 28.00 multiplied by 14, divided by 30: 13.0667 |

**Method 2** — patient pay 15.00, club 30-day price 4.00: a short fill of 30 days supply gives 15.00 less 4.00, which is 11.00; a short fill of 31 days gives 15.00 less 8.00, which is 7.00.

**Method 3** — patient pay 18.00, 40 units dispensed, 20 owed: 18.00 multiplied by 20, divided by 60, which is 6.00.

A cash fill, a discount-program fill without an active Savings Club membership, and an insurance-billed fill whose active coverage is another plan class all take method 3.
